newsitem.title: SWEDEN: EU did not block Boeing/McDonnell merger-spokesman.
newsitem.headline: EU did not block Boeing/McDonnell merger-spokesman.

text.p: A European Commission spokesman on Monday denied a media report that the commission's competition policy authority had decided it would block a proposed merger between Boeing Corp and McDonnell Douglas Corp .
A spokesman for Karel Van Miert, who heads competition policy in the European Union, told a conference call that Van Miert had not said the commission's competition authority would block the merger.
But Van Miert had called for changes in the merger proposal, the spokesman said.
"As far as the longterm exclusive contracts are concerned, they are totally unacceptable, Van Miert said in Stockholm," the spokesman said. "But that is nothing new."
Swedish national news agency TT said on Monday that Van Mert had said the commission had blocked the merger. Later in the day, it corrected the story, saying no decision had been taken.
The European Commission launched a full probe on March 13 on the Boeing-McDonnell deal, which will create a group with $48 billion in annual sales.
The commission is reviewing the proposal and will issue a so-called statement of objections by the end of May.
It has four months or until about mid-July to complete its investigation and to decide whether to clear it or block it.
A major industry concern over a merged Boeing/McDonnell lies in the greater leverage the group would have in negotiating exclusive contracts with airlines.
This is a worry already voiced by Van Miert, following Boeing deals agreed by Delta Air Lines and AMR Corp.'s American Airlines.

When launching the probe in March the commission said it would in particular have to examine to what extent Boeing's leading position in the market for commercial jet aircraft could be strengthened by the proposed merger.
The alliance is also being investigated by the U.S. Federal Trade Commission.
